added_claim_errors: Describes the no-penalty exception as applying to coverage "from an employer with 20+ employees": imprecise, because employer size is not a condition of the SEP (it decides who pays first). Minor.
"a few plans do [require Part B] for certain employee classes": unverifiable, no source given.
"coverage generally starts the month after Social Security processes your form": imprecise. SEP coverage starts the month after sign-up (or a chosen later month), not after processing.
Premium given as "roughly $185–$210/month" rather than the 2026 figure of $202.90: vague, though not wrong.

The Part B penalty "applies to people who go without creditable coverage": misleading. The Part B exemption needs a group health plan based on current employment. 'Creditable coverage' is a Part D idea, and retiree or COBRA coverage would not protect against the Part B penalty.

Tells the asker to apply at retirement "using CMS-40B plus CMS-L564" with no condition, after advising HSA holders to skip Part A. CMS-40B is wrong for someone without Part A; they must apply for A and B together through SSA.
"sign up for Part D within 63 days": imprecise. The Part D SEP runs 2 full months after coverage ends; 63 days is the penalty threshold.
Links penalty-free delay to being "above the 20-employee threshold": imprecise, because size is not an SEP condition. Minor.

reasons: Both answers correct the premise at the start and tell the asker to hold off on Part B. Both give sound HR questions and auto-enrollment guidance, and both miss the exception for a job that ends during the IEP. A is more complete. It explains that Part A is backdated up to 6 months, which matters for an HSA, and that Part B starts the Medigap window. It also says to apply the month before coverage ends and names CMS-L564. B leaves out the HSA backdating risk and Medigap entirely. B also adds two errors: it frames the Part B penalty as depending on 'creditable coverage', and it recommends CMS-40B without conditions even for someone who deferred Part A. Neither gives the exact $202.90 premium. A is somewhat longer but still easy to act on.
